By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE:

The People Operations team builds the infrastructure that lets Hadrian scale. We are hiring a People Strategy & Planning Manager  to own how Hadrian decides who we hire, when, and why. Headcount is the single biggest input into our growth, and getting it right means running a real program: a planning cycle the business trusts, a clear line from program demand to approved roles, and one number that Finance, Recruiting, and the business all agree on.

This is a program management job at its core, and the hard part is not the spreadsheet. It is holding a cross-functional cycle together across People, Recruiting, Finance, Engineering and Program leadership, each with their own pressures and their own view of what the plan should say. You will get people aligned, keep the plan honest as it changes, and land the change management so the process actually gets adopted instead of worked around.

You know how to structure an ambiguous problem, run a cycle to a deadline, and build the artifact that moves a decision forward. You live with the outcome, and you have to bring people with you.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the headcount planning program end to end. Run our planning cycles from both directions, bottoms-up from the business and tops-down from leadership, then consolidate into one plan that holds up to scrutiny.

 - Partner with our engineering and program leadership to turn program demand signal into role-level headcount needs, so the plan reflects what we actually have to build rather than a generic growth curve.

 - Work side by side with Finance to cost the plan, reconcile it against budget, and produce a single forecasted headcount picture that everyone works from.

 - Hand that plan cleanly to Recruiting Operations so approved roles land in our systems as requisitions recruiters can act on, with the data structured well enough to report on.

 - Program manage the recurring monthly cadence with our embedded People Partners and Recruiting Leads, including how program and assignment tagging gets reconciled and loaded, so we can see our workforce by program and not just by department.

 - Partner with Workplace Services as our footprint expands, so hiring plans and physical capacity are planned together rather than discovered out of sync.

 - Drive the change management. Build the cadence, the intake, the artifacts, and the communications that make this a program people rely on, and keep raising the bar on it each cycle.

 - Bring structure and visibility to leadership. Know the status of the plan at any moment, flag risk early, and make the tradeoffs legible to executives making the call.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 7+ years of experience spanning management consulting or a similar structured problem-solving environment, plus time in-house where you owned a program and lived with the results.

 - Exceptional stakeholder management. You build credibility fast with senior leaders, you can hold a line without damaging the relationship, and you understand the nuance of influencing people who do not report to you and will still be in the room next quarter.

 - Strong project management fundamentals. You work from a plan, you drive to dates, you manage dependencies across functions, and nothing quietly falls through the cracks.

 - Real change management experience. You have rolled out a process that changed how people work, and you have handled the resistance, the adoption gap, and the comms that go with it.

 - Comfort with planning data and financial mechanics. You can build and pressure-test a workforce model, reconcile it against a budget, and explain the delta in plain language.

 - Executive-grade communication. You can write the one-pager that gets a decision made and run the meeting where it happens.

 - High adaptability. You are energized by shifting scope, and you bring structure to ambiguity rather than waiting for it to be handed to you.


WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

 - You have run a workforce or headcount planning cycle before in close partnership with Finance, and you know where these processes usually break.

 - You have worked in a high-growth, operationally intense environment such as startup, manufacturing, defense, or similar, where you had to build the program while the business moved at full speed.

 - You are hands-on with the systems layer, including HRIS, ATS, and headcount planning tools such as ChartHop, exceland you understand that a program is only as good as the data flowing through it.

 - You have supported engineering or technical organizations and can hold your own in a conversation about what a program actually needs.

 - You see People and headcount planning as a lever for business performance, not a support function that reacts to requests.


COMPENSATION

For this role, the target salary range is 200,000 - 240,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

 - Flexible vacation policy

HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE:

Growth Finance owns the economics of how Hadrian wins work. We sit at the front end of every program — pricing the pursuit, shaping the deal, and structuring the partnerships and joint ventures that get new capacity off the ground with our commercial and government customers. The Associate is the analytical center of that work. You'll build the model behind a pursuit from a blank sheet: unit economics, capacity and capex requirements, rate and margin structure, and the returns case that determines whether we bid, at what price, and on what terms. You'll pressure-test your own assumptions before anyone else gets the chance, and you'll be expected to have a view — not just a spreadsheet — on whether a program is worth pursuing.

Beyond the model, you'll help structure the vehicles. That means partnership and JV economics, term sheets, waterfall and downside mechanics, and the diligence behind counterparties we're considering taking risk with. You'll write the memo that goes to leadership, and you'll defend it in the room.

This is a small team with a short path to owning deals outright. The work available to you scales with what you demonstrate rather than with tenure.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and own financial models for Hadrian's largest capital decisions — factory builds, new capability investments across welding, casting, forging, and additive, and program-level spend. This includes scenario modeling, cash flow forecasting, and spend projections.

 - Own the financial evaluation of individual investments end to end, applying transaction-level rigor: ROI, payback period, cash impact, and the explicit trade-offs across cost, schedule, and scope.

 - Support corporate development and capital markets work spanning M&A, carve-outs, equity investments, and joint ventures — from market research and target screening through diligence, structuring, and modeling.

 - Act as the financial counterpart to engineering, manufacturing, and program leadership. Many initiatives reach you as an engineering idea and a number on a whiteboard; you bring visibility, structure, and accountability.

 - Maintain forecasts and consolidated budgets that tie to our accounting frameworks, and keep financial plans aligned to operational milestones and program timelines.

 - Provide real-time insight into program performance — surfacing risks, opportunities, and trade-offs early enough for someone to act on them.

 - Analyze the operational drivers that determine whether a factory is economic: labor productivity, machine utilization, throughput, and unit cost performance.

 - Translate analysis into executive- and board-facing materials. Your work will be read by people who decide in minutes, so the "so what" has to survive compression.

 - Improve the plumbing. Find and fix gaps in reporting, forecasting process, automation, and data infrastructure rather than building workarounds.

 - Work across functions constantly — Production Operations, Engineering, Program Management, Special Projects, Automation, Accounting, Legal, and Investor Relations.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 2-5 years experience across strategic finance, FP&A, investment banking, private equity or growth equity, private credit, management consulting, corporate development, and/or strategy & operations.

 - Ability to build a complex financial model from a blank page — not only to maintain one you inherited. Cash flow forecasting and scenario analysis are core, not adjacent.

 - Demonstrated ability to carry ambiguous, cross-functional work all the way to a decision without being managed to it. We would rather tell you to slow down than to speed up.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, specifically the ability to compress a complex analysis into something a senior leader can act on immediately.

 - High ownership and genuine curiosity about how physical things get made. Comfort being wrong in public, and iterating quickly when you are.

 - Ability to manage multiple concurrent work streams without dropping any of them.

 - U.S. Person status is required, as this position needs access to export-controlled data.


WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

 - Experience in capital-intensive industries — aerospace and defense, advanced manufacturing, automotive, semiconductors, energy, or data centers.

 - Project finance, capital project analysis, or large-scale infrastructure and high-dollar investment work.

 - M&A due diligence, transaction structuring, carve-outs, transaction advisory, or restructuring.

 - Exposure to program management or large-scale project delivery.

 - Experience in a high-growth or PE/VC-backed environment.

 - Working knowledge of government contracting processes and procedures.

 - NetSuite or comparable ERP experience.
